courseTitle: Ionic - Build iOS, Android & Web Apps with Ionic & Angular

lectures.title: Storing Auth Data in Device Storag

cues.en: I want to store the token and I want to store it either in my in-browser storage on a Mac or on a
PC but on a real device, I want to store it on that real device because if I would use the
in-browser storage, that would be available in that wrapped web app
the Ionic app is but it might be cleared by the wrapping app shell and it's less reliable than our on
device storage and therefore on the native device, I want to use that on-device storage and Capacitor
conveniently gives us access to that storage here, under that storage plugin and there, we see we should
use that instead of using local storage which would be our normal alternative in web APIs and you
can also see that this of course is not meant for high performance data as you see,
you might want to have a look at SQL lite if you need that but it's great for storing key-value data
as we have it here.
So let's go back to our auth service now because that is where I now also want to store data in the
storage
and of course also retrieve it when our application starts. For that, I'll first of all add a new private
method in the auth service which I name store auth data and I want to store things like the
userId and the token and important, also the token expiration date,
so token expiration date because we need to store that to find out whether the token still is valid
when we come back at a later point of time, when we reload this app, we need to check whether that token
we store is still is valid and we can do so with the help of that token expiration date.
Now next, I want to use Capacitor in here,
so therefore I'll import something from @capacitor/core and that something is the same thing we used
before,
that would be our plugins object. Now in store data, store auth data, I'll use plugin or plugins, excuse
me, storage and then there, we have our various methods for interacting with the storage,
for example here we need the set method. The set method allows us to store a key-value pair and we have
to pass an object to set where we defined a key and then also the value we want to store for that key
and later, we can retrieve data by that key.
Now the key here could be just auth data, should be a string though, auth data and the value should
be a string and therefore I'll merge these three fields into a stringified object. So I'll create
a new data constant,
that will be a Javascript object where I have my userId, stored in a userId property, tokens stored
in the token property and token expiration date stored in a token expiration date property.
Now this is a Javascript object and we can't store an object in there,
we need to store a string, conveniently we can use JSON stringify to turn that object into a string
in JavaScript and then it's that data string which I'm storing here in the end.
So this stores data, we of course also want to retrieve data
however, not just store it but first of all, let's use our store auth data method. Here, set user data looks
like a good place because this is in the end what we call for both signing up and logging in.
So in set user data when we emit our new user, we can also call this store auth data and there, we now forward
user data localId which is that userId, user data token, idToken which is that token and that
expiration time we're creating there,
we also forward that but since I need a string, we call to ISO string here.
Now we're storing data,
let's next focus on retrieving that data.
